answer.origin: Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool, Aug 1 2026 article on Nvidia and Alphabet revenue trends (third-party media report; Nvidia figures attributed to company filings with data as of July 31, 2026)

findings.claim: Nvidia's reported quarterly revenue rose in each sequential quarter in the article's series, from $30.0 billion (period ended July 2024) to $81.6 billion (period ended April 2026).
findings.use: Supports a reading that Nvidia's reported revenue grew sequentially across the eight quarters shown, which is the company's own reported trend rather than a forecast.
findings.grounds: The figures are reported by a media outlet that attributes them to company filings. The article gives no direct filing reference, and the series interleaves Alphabet figures, so attribution depends on matching the Nvidia values to the Nvidia text. The uncertainty that matters is whether the period labels and figures match Nvidia's own filings, not whether growth occurred.
findings.next_check: Verify each Nvidia quarterly revenue figure and its period label against Nvidia's 10-Q and 10-K filings for the quarters from July 2024 through April 2026.

findings.claim: Nvidia's most recent quarter, the quarter ended April 26, 2026, reported a net income margin of 72%.
findings.use: Supports a limited reading of Nvidia's reported profitability for that quarter. It does not establish that the margin will persist or explain its drivers.
findings.grounds: The margin is stated in a media article that cites company filings and gives no computation. The article does not provide the net income or revenue inputs for that quarter, so the figure can be reported but not independently recomputed from the text.
findings.next_check: Compare the 72% figure with the net income and revenue reported in Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended April 26, 2026, and check whether any one-time items affected net income.

findings.claim: Nvidia's most recent quarter revenue was $81.6 billion, and the company forecast revenue of $91 billion for the next quarter, continuing the acceleration.
findings.use: Supports a conditional view that management expects further sequential revenue growth into the next quarter. The forecast is a company expectation, not a realized result.
findings.grounds: The $81.6 billion figure is reported from company filings, while the $91 billion figure is a management forecast relayed by a media outlet. The article does not give the guidance date, the basis for the forecast, or the assumptions behind it, so the uncertainty that matters is whether the forecast was made on the terms the article implies.
findings.next_check: Check the original Nvidia guidance statement for the $91 billion next-quarter forecast, including its date and any stated assumptions, and compare it with the reported revenue in the following earnings release.

findings.claim: Nvidia's new Vera Rubin AI platform is expected to contribute to ongoing sales growth.
findings.use: Leads to an investigation of whether the Vera Rubin product ramp is the driver of Nvidia's forecast growth. The article gives no quantified contribution or timing.
findings.grounds: The statement is a media expectation without a direct quote from Nvidia or a quantified contribution. The article ties the platform to the forecast only by implication, so the causal link between Vera Rubin and the forecast remains unresolved.
findings.next_check: Look for Nvidia management commentary or filings that quantify the Vera Rubin contribution to revenue, along with the expected shipment or production timing.

findings.use: Leads to an investigation of whether Alphabet is a material Nvidia customer and of the scale of any customer concentration. The article does not establish the size of the relationship.
findings.grounds: The article states the customer relationship without quantification, contract terms, or a source. The relationship is named, but its size, timing and share of Nvidia revenue are unresolved, so it cannot support any conclusion about revenue concentration.
findings.next_check: Check Nvidia's 10-Q and 10-K customer concentration disclosures to see whether Alphabet is named or whether it exceeds the disclosed concentration thresholds.

findings.claim: Alphabet's Google Cloud revenue grew 82% year over year to $24.8 billion in Q2, its backlog rose to over $500 billion from $462 billion in Q1, and Alphabet reported a 94% net income margin for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Securities fraud investigations were announced against Alphabet in July 2026.
findings.use: Reject for this research: these claims concern Alphabet, which is outside the covered company scope of NVDA.
findings.grounds: The research scope covers only NVDA. The Alphabet cloud, backlog, margin and legal-investigation claims do not bear on Nvidia's business and are not used to support a finding about it.
